what: frame's ceil-division -(-L // 16) wraps when L is a numpy uint64, giving wrong symbol counts.
evidence: review:frame: _data_symbols(np.uint64(4096)) gives 4352, not 4370; FrameSpec(n_data=np.uint64(4096)).n_sym is 7652; lframe._data_symbols(np.uint64(2048), 1320) gives 0. Suggested fix: int(L).

what: beaconfile.write opens and truncates the target before to_bytes validates. A refused BeaconFile therefore empties an existing good file; the C++ reproduces this deliberately.
evidence: port:picture_chain notes.

what: picture.to_int8 relies on numpy's platform-defined NaN-to-int8 cast. The C++ pins NaN to 0.
evidence: port:picture_chain notes.

what: ce.to_audio's phase reduction overflows int64 for large denominators and offsets. The same wrap exists in lwave.mix_turns for a huge period. Neither is reachable for normal slots, and the C++ uses an exact mulmod.
evidence: (nn*(num % period)) % period wraps when den > ~380k with large or negative n0; mix_turns wraps for a period past ~3e9 (e.g. f_hz=-0.1 at fs=250); normal slots have n0 < 1.5e7.

what: ce.PULSE_TABLE is computed at import with numpy trig, while the C++ uses a frozen table. The two could differ by an ulp on another platform.
evidence: port:ce_tx notes.

what: ce.phase_at is discontinuous at every whole-symbol tau, because the pulse is cut at +-8 symbols with a nonzero step. Chunking a very long pass off-grid therefore changes the audio. No preset reaches this.
evidence: Step p(8)=0.006; jumps up to 0.0199 rad (0.003-0.005 rad at tau 1000/5000). Off-grid chunking differs by up to 7.4e-3 at amplitude 0.5 over 602 samples. Needs a piece starting more than 16,384,005 samples (~2048 s; exact threshold 2048.000625 s) after t0.

what: ce.cw_phase_turns with a NaN tau subtracts every window through searchsorted. The C++ records this as a deviation and does not copy it.
evidence: port:ce_tx notes.

what: Python receive_slot on noise-free TINY/l-tiny audio returns spurious extra passes from grating-lobe candidates and is very slow, so the chain tests add -6 dB of noise.
evidence: review:integrate / integrate notes.

what: wavio's int16 writer uses an unspecified cast for out-of-range floats, which only happens with peak > 1.
evidence: pass_audio notes; C++ maps NaN to int16 0.

what: PIL clips 16-bit PNGs (I;16) at 255, so Python and the native stb decoder produce different pictures from the same file.
evidence: Picture ID 90cb2490 from Python against 231e67e5 native.

what: lframe.py carries a stale 'pending Jeff's call' comment.
evidence: port:frame; plan section 4.6.

evidence: Map: the exception sets done.

evidence: Map notes.

evidence: Map notes.

evidence: Map notes.

what: The CLIs disagree with each other.
evidence: Map: qrss_simulate --ook on a .bin overrides the FSK flag where qrss_transmit refuses; qrss_simulate ignores --post for WAV input; --frame takes CE names only in transmit and simulate, both in receive, any in listen; precision defaults are fp16 for encode and fp32 for receive/decode/listen.

what: The GUI hand-copies QRSS constants, and one of them was wrong.
evidence: Map: PASS_S 1782.7 against 1782.678125; FREQ_MIN 300 Hz, too low for L's 322.07; MARK_L constants. PASS_S was fixed in 2b6d29b, which takes constants from the generated config.

what: Two Python tests are expected failures.
evidence: Map: E3 duplicate member attached by correlation; strict xfail M5 80 Hz skirt measured -60.4 dB against a design of -65.

what: lwave.resample's filter is designed for 8 kHz whatever fs_out is.
evidence: Map notes.

what: scipy 1.18.1's make_lsq_spline returns finite but wrong coefficients when early data points are sparse before a gap, because its qr_reduce skips rows with offset[i] > i. PathFn only checks that the coefficients are finite, so it silently uses the wrong spline as the frequency path; the port reproduces this bit-exactly.
evidence: Least-squares residual is 10^2 to 10^5 times the optimum in 1324 of 2000 targeted random trials (scratchpad sweep). The guard is the finite check in sstvae/qrss/track.py PathFn. A residual check, or dropping knots that have no data, would catch it in both implementations.

what: np.linalg.eigh returns NaN for NaN input without raising, so the tracker's `except LinAlgError` fallbacks never fire on that path and the NaN propagates.
evidence: measured: np.linalg.eigh(np.array([[nan,0],[0,1]])) returns NaN with no exception

what: PathFn([nan]) raises ValueError, and two or more NaN times, or all times zero, raise LinAlgError from polyfit. Neither is caught, so a detection with a bad path takes down the caller instead of being skipped.
evidence: PathFn([nan]) gives 'cannot convert float NaN to integer'; the NaN-times and zero-times cases give 'SVD did not converge'. Pinned in native/tests/qrss/test_trackbase.cpp test_pathfn refusals; inferred from sstvae/qrss/track.py.

what: PathFn.__init__ never checks that len(f) == len(w) == len(t): it indexes f and w by argsort(t), so a longer f or w is silently truncated and a shorter one raises an IndexError naming an internal index.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/track.py:255-259 (skeleton review); no current caller trips it

what: With repeated times the reference PathFn is not reproducible across hosts. np.argsort's default kind is unstable, and numpy 2.x dispatches it to x86-simd-sort kernels by CPU feature, so the order of equal times and the spline coefficients can differ between AVX-512 and non-AVX-512 machines.
evidence: inferred from code (track.py:258 np.argsort(t)); measured ~5e-12 coefficient differences against the stable C++ order

what: blank() of 1 to 100 FE samples raises ValueError 'array of sample points is empty' instead of passing through. With hop=200, running_median's centres are empty for n <= 100, so a capture of up to 25 ms crashes the blanker.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/frontend.py running_median (centres = np.arange(hop // 2, max(n, 1), hop)) and _interp_to_samples; tests/test_qrss_native_frontend.py::test_blank_refuses_what_the_reference_does pins it for n in (1, 50, 100); the C++ keeps the behaviour

what: A negative `chunk` makes `range(0, n, chunk)` empty, and four functions then return without raising: running_median, normalise and _interp_to_samples (frontend) and acquire.spectrogram return their uninitialised np.empty buffers, while ce.matched_filter and lwave.matched_filter return all zeros. Separately, acquire.spectrogram raises "object of type 'numpy.int64' has no len()" for a 0-d starts.
evidence: inferred from code: frontend.py chunk loops over np.empty outputs; acquire.py:246-258; ce.py:483-500, lwave.py:367; tests/test_qrss_native_ce_rx.py test_matched_filter_chunks_and_positions. chunk=0 raises from range(). Nothing passes a chunk today.

what: _noise_response, _fold_power and _fe_power are lru_cached but return writeable arrays, unlike _fe_flat and _fe_response. A caller that modifies one in place silently corrupts the cache for every later noise_psd call with the same arguments.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/frontend.py:293-337 (no writeable=False) against :351 and :364 (writeable=False)

what: scipy.ndimage.median_filter's 1-D fast path reads one element past the array when the window is exactly 2n+1 (lim2 == 0). Tie-breaking, and NaN results, then depend on whatever memory follows the array; the receiver cannot reach this.
evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_ndfilter.py::test_nan_follows_scipy failed for (n=2, w=5) before that case was excluded: [nan, nan] from scipy vs [nan, 0.659] from its own generic path. Unreachable because spectral_shape clamps w to at most n_bins, so lim2 > 0.

what: Given an explicit n, np.fft.irfft(empty, n) reads x[0] past the end of the input and returns garbage instead of raising. The port refuses.
evidence: numpy 2.5.3 _pocketfft_umath.cpp irfft_loop copies x[0] unconditionally; without n numpy raises 'Invalid number of FFT data points (-2)'; native/core/math/npfft.cpp irfft_impl refuses

what: For a strong preamble, gammaincc underflows to 0 at every scale and np.argmin ties to scale 0 (g=1, the fully noncoherent statistic). preamble_search then refines df/tau on that surface whatever scale carries the signal; the 'p underflows' branch picks the cell by lam2 but not the scale. Wave 5 found that ordinary strong signals reach this branch.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/acquire.py:852-857. Wave 4 math: a planted ctest cell with Lambda about 800 at all four scales gives p = 0 and best = 0. Wave 5 A1/A2 review: A2 Lambda saturates at about 620 for CE from about 0 dB SNR, and pmin < 1e-250 at 0 and 10 dB (probe2.py); the C++ takes the same branch.

what: demod.extract and ldemod.extract_l mutate their argument by setting track.m = np.asarray(m). EM re-extraction relies on this, but extracting twice with different m from one TrackResult leaves the second m behind; the binding reproduces the mutation.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/demod.py:245-246, ldemod.py:326-327; test_extract_with_given_m_replaces_the_tracks; replace_m in demod_rx.hpp

what: frame.spread_signs checks only the shape of hdr_bits, although its error text says 'values of 0/1'. Bits of 2 silently give a sign of -3, so a header-decode bug producing non-binary bits would corrupt round B's spread subtraction with no error; frame.assemble does validate values.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/frame.py:302-308 against :338; probe: hdr_bits=2*kb gives values from ldemod.data_estimates_l

what: Given an L spec, ce.mean_template, _mean_template_grid, phase_at and at_positions have no waveform guard. They fail deep in frame.layout with a misleading assertion about header slots.
evidence: The assertion reads "1237 header slots for 2474 bits". sstvae/qrss/ce.py:124-128 and frame.py:271-280. The receiver never calls them this way.

what: The reference is inconsistently strict about track field types. CE demod.symbol_estimates indexes tr.m/u/P/N/psi directly, so a list raises TypeError, while ldemod.symbol_estimates_l wraps every field in np.asarray, so a list works.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/demod.py:71-73 against ldemod.py:158-159; matters only for hand-built stubs

what: known_symbols did not check the header bits' length. A short header silently returned a _Known whose pos and val differ in length, while make_classes on the same input raises.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/track.py:454-463; probe: known_symbols(SHORT, bits[:-1]) -> pos (3574,), val (3573,). Fixed in wave 7 (commit ce73aff: known_symbols takes its values from make_classes and refuses a short header with make_classes' error).

what: derotate(chan, fn) with an fn that returns a scalar, such as a constant frequency, fails inside np.interp instead of broadcasting. Only array-valued paths work.
evidence: np.interp raises 'fp and xp are not of the same length.'. sstvae/qrss/track.py:303-313: a scalar g gives a cumsum of length 1, then np.interp runs over n indices. Every current caller passes a PathFn.

what: refine_timing's 3-D (gamma) Newton branch is never taken by any fixture or simulated pass, so it is untested in the reference as well as the port.
evidence: measured: MEDIUM at -6 dB with tx_ppm -30: branch evaluated on 3 tracks, never taken (zk(th3) > zk(th) + 1 never holds). Injected gamma 3/-6: not taken. 12/25/-40: None on both sides.

what: verify's blind path computed the coarse timing grid twice on the same z_d and path: once inside verify_track (n_best 1) and again for the runners-up (n_best=V_TIMING_TRIES). Sharing the fit roughly halves the blind gate's cost on a weak candidate.
evidence: In sstvae/qrss/track.py verify(), the verify_track(... fit=fit) call is followed by fit_timing(..., n_best=V_TIMING_TRIES) with the same fn and z_d. Fixed in wave 7 (commit ce73aff, _fit_timing_tries: one grid for both, covering verify and verify_l).

what: verify keeps the first base's Z_ref with `if best is None or alt.z_ref > best.z_ref`. If that first Z_ref is NaN, every later comparison is False, so _flat_path and line_path can never be chosen; the C++ copies this.
evidence: inferred from code, sstvae/qrss/track.py verify (base loop); latent: an all-erased frame gives 0.0, not NaN

what: _segment_timing's single-segment fallback fits with the outer `delta`, not the loop's `d_`. This is harmless today, but anyone who reorders that walk will hit it.
evidence: inferred from code, sstvae/qrss/track.py _segment_timing; d_ only diverges after the ptp >= 300 ppm refusal, which never reaches the single-segment fit (branch coverage via scratchpad lines.py tracer)

what: fit_timing's two correlation paths (FFT when nlag > 64, direct otherwise) disagree at the capture's end: one zero-extends an interpolation pair that straddles len(x), the other drops it. Only receiver.channel_for's padding hides this, so an unpadded capture, for example from a future live path, would get a timing that depends on the search width.
evidence: inferred from code plus probe: test_probe_fit_timing_random local searches on both sides of the 64-lag switch agree only on padded captures

what: _cell_line indexes stat[d0, b] first and indexes the requested drift d only if it survives the straight-drift comparison. An out-of-range d with a low v therefore succeeds, and whether a bad drift index is noticed depends on the statistic's value.
evidence: A._cell_line(cs, 0, 13, 10.0) succeeds; inferred from sstvae/qrss/acquire.py _cell_line

what: Some return types depend on the value. CarrierCandidate.f_hz is np.float64 when refined from a cell but a Python float when hint_line falls back to the hint, and _phase_line's slope is np.float64 only when fitted.
evidence: inferred from sstvae/qrss/acquire.py hint_line/_phase_line; the binding mirrors it (cell_to_py)

what: _phase_line divides by sxx without a guard. A degenerate input (all chunks at one time, or zero weight spread) emits a RuntimeWarning and returns a NaN slope.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/acquire.py:823 RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in scalar divide' during test_fine_sums_coherent_phase_line

what: track_before_detect with a band narrower than its clip span returns a confident hit at the wrong frequency. np.clip is called with a_min > a_max, the negative slice bounds wrap, and bins are read from the wrong end of the grid. The port author called this the serious one of the three A3 bugs; the C++ refuses with NotImplementedError.
evidence: Probe: band (1000, 1060), candidate 1030 Hz -> hit centre 1020 Hz, path 1046.5-1050.75 Hz (sstvae/qrss/acquire.py, the band clip in track_before_detect/l_pilot_bins)

what: tbd_viterbi with B < |max_step| < 2B (B bins) fails with an opaque numpy broadcast ValueError instead of a parameter error. With |max_step| >= 2B it silently behaves differently, so the valid step range is undocumented and unchecked.
evidence: Probe of tbd_viterbi with an 81-bin E and max_step 100 -> ValueError 'operands could not be broadcast together'

what: _path_line on a path with fewer than 2 points raises UnboundLocalError, because the refit branch references a variable assigned only inside the loop. A degenerate path that reaches TbdHit.f_hz crashes instead of giving NaN or a clear error.
evidence: Probe: A._path_line(FreqPath with 1 point) -> UnboundLocalError; mirrored as acquire::UnboundLocal and pinned in test_acquire_tbd.cpp

what: drop_symbol_rate_aliases requires an alias's timing to be within T/2 (15.2 ms). On a 0 dB CE signal hinted at f-1/T, a passed alias 19.4 ms off was kept, so the acquisition reported two CE preamble hits for one signal (the +1/T alias, 12.6 ms off, was dropped). This shows only when a hint or an A1 line lands on the alias; gate V then has to reject it.

An L hint within 2.5 Hz of a failed L hit at an A1 line reuses that hit (near[0]) and is never searched at the hint itself, so a hint's outcome depends on unrelated A1 lines. Probably intended. The reviewer adds that h.passed is always False on that branch, so the lookup only saves one A2 search.
evidence: probe_band.py on TL._capture(l-short, 1203.4, 0 dB, seed 10): a hint at the -1/T_L alias 1186.9 Hz (A1 line at 1184.95 Hz) is never searched there. A hint at 1188.0 reaches it, and it passes A2-L with p about 1e-22.

what: acquire() failed as a whole on one bad hint: a NaN or inf frequency raised ValueError or OverflowError from inside A2, losing the whole slot's acquisition. Wave 7 item 3 now drops non-finite hints, including inside an (f, waveform) tuple, before A2, in Python and C++.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/acquire.py:1569-1573 (test_acquire_odd_hints). Wave 7: a NaN or inf hint mixed with good ones gives exactly the good hints' result in both implementations; mutation-checked in Python and in acquire.cpp.

what: The single-frame path does not reject an (f, waveform) hint; it fails by accident. The error depends on whether A2 produced hits. The C++ needs tuple_hint(have_hits) to match.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/acquire.py:1566-1569: "unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'float' and 'tuple'" when there are hits, else "float() argument must be ... not 'tuple'"; the stubbed fuzz hits both messages

what: refine_timing_l on a finished track is not a fixed point. It refines against tr.u_pl/P_pl, which were computed under the pre-refinement timing, so calling it again moves tau0. Harmless inside track_l's loop.
evidence: tau0 +0.915 CH samples on l-short round A, -0.583 on l-tiny round A

what: ltrack's layout-using functions (_Model, _distortion, data_templates, _pilot_gain, pilot_wave, _lead_supported_l) do not check the waveform. Given a CE frame, lframe.layout fails in one of two unrelated ways. An explicit _l_only guard would give one clear message.
evidence: AttributeError (no n_data_payload) or AssertionError '<n> header symbols for 2474 bits', with n = n_hdr - ceil(n_hdr/16); probed on TINY and FULL CE specs

what: With a scalar tau, pilot_wave and _pilot_gain are inconsistent: _pilot_gain returns np.float64, but pilot_wave raises TypeError because lwave.pilot's _ramp_envelope item-assigns into a 0-d result.
evidence: pilot_wave(3.5, L_SHORT) raises TypeError; _pilot_gain(3.5, L_SHORT) gives np.float64(0.656)

what: test_qrss_live's end-of-slot-in-a-child test compared a spawned pure-Python child with the in-process implementation using exact equality. Under --native-qrss it therefore asserted bitwise track/track_timing, which their contracts do not claim, and it had failed since wave 5. The 6a follow-ups hold it to the port's tolerance under --native-qrss and keep it bitwise otherwise.
evidence: Bisect: only track gives dz=9.31e-10 and df=-2.0e-12; only track_timing gives dz=9.31e-10; every other rx module is exact (livebisect.py). Fixed in 40c3910.

what: _segment_timing_l's inner fit() uses the enclosing delta (the function argument) in its short-span branch, ab - tp * sps * (1 + delta), instead of its own d_ parameter. This is the same latent bug as CE's _segment_timing; the port reproduces it.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/ltrack.py _segment_timing_l, fit()

what: verify_l computed the blind coarse grid twice on the same z_d: verify_track_l's own blind fit, then fit_timing_l again with n_best=V_TIMING_TRIES for the runners-up. Fixed in wave 7 item 5 in both implementations, bit-identically.
evidence: About 13 s of duplicated Python work on L FULL and about 1.5 s in C++ (6a estimate). See the wave 7 performance item for the measured saving.

what: L's _segment_timing_l scores its final statistic through the ok mask (terms past x count 0), while CE's _segment_timing does not. The two waveforms' scores therefore differ near capture edges. An asymmetry, not a crash.
evidence: ltrack.py _segment_timing_l stat() vs track.py _segment_timing

what: fit_timing_l's FFT path (above 64 lags) and its direct path disagree on an interpolation pair straddling an end of x. The FFT path keeps the inside half and the direct path drops the term. This happens at both ends (x[-1],x[0] and x[len-1],x[len]), not only at the end as wave 5 recorded for CE. The receiver cannot reach it, because channel_for zero-pads (about 13.5 s before t0 against the blind search's 2.5 s, and 3 s past the farthest lag).
evidence: test_probe_fit_timing_l_unpadded: unpadded, the FFT gap is > 1e-3 of scale (about 1.4% of the grid's scale at those cells), while C++ against direct is 1.95e-15. Padded, C++ against FFT is 3.4e-14. Padding pinned by test_receiver_channel_holds_every_lag.

what: verify/verify_l track best + tries[1:], assuming tries[0] is the timing already tracked. On L noise it is not: a carrier estimate's runner-up outscores every first peak after segment refinement, so n_best=1's timing is tms[1]. The best timing is then tracked twice and the strongest runner-up never. Kept for bit-identity and pinned. Worth a look in the reference.
evidence: 6a review inferred it from the code. Wave 7 measured it: sstvae/qrss/track.py:1450, ltrack.py:1301. test_fit_timing_tries_l asserts {('reference','noise',V),('native','noise',V)} are in the split set; cands[2:] are pinned bitwise to fit_timing(n_best=1) + fit_timing(n_best=V)[1:].

what: _clock_phase computes its factor in the dtype of d, so a float32 d would give a float32 phase (callers pass a Python float). A negative sig2 makes math.sqrt raise in Python but gives NaN in the C++. Unreachable, because sig2 is a variance.
evidence: Inferred from code: sstvae/qrss/ltrack.py _clock_phase and _segment_timing_l

what: Porting flagged PassResult.cw.agrees as possibly np.bool_ (from z > Z_ACCEPT), which json.dumps rejects. Wave 7 item 1 wraps it in bool(). The review found the premise false: cwid.match has returned a Python float since wave 4, so the bool() is defensive.
evidence: Wave 6b: inferred from code, receiver.py _cw_result. Wave 7 review: removing bool() still passed the builder's test. The rewritten test_pass_fields_are_plain_json stubs match to return np.float64.

what: _receive_pass_l did not check its frame's waveform (only receive_pass did). A direct caller with a CE frame got the obscure "AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fs'". Wave 7 item 2 makes it give receive_pass's refusal, as the C++ row receive_pass does.
evidence: sstvae/qrss/receiver.py:330; tests/test_qrss_lreceiver.py::test_receive_pass_l_refuses_a_frame_that_is_not_l

what: _suspect_neighbour never fires on any simulated signal, including the weak-neighbour and alias captures built to provoke it; only the stubbed fuzz reaches it. Either it guards a field case the simulator cannot make, or it is dead. A recorded capture should decide before anyone relies on it.
evidence: test_scenarios_reach_the_rules hit counts; test_slot_orchestration_stubbed fuzz hit counts

what: _owned unpacks a3 entries lazily, so a malformed entry after the deciding line is never noticed. Harmless today, because a3 comes from _a3_lines. The C++ binding was made lazy to match.
evidence: Inferred from code; pinned in test_rules_refusals and test_owned_walks_a3_lazily

what: scipy.io.wavfile.read (under wavio.read_wav) misreads 8-bit PCM in a container wider than one byte. It reads n_samples contiguous single bytes, returning the first half (or third, ...) of the raw bytes, and leaves the file position mid-chunk, misaligning the chunk walk. The C++ reproduces this on purpose.
evidence: scipy/io/wavfile.py:492-493 and :515-516; corner case pcm-8in2 and ctest u8in2.wav: data ff 00 80 00 reads [1.0, 0.0]

what: scipy.io.wavfile misaligns its chunk walk after any data chunk whose size is not a multiple of the container. A writer that leaves an odd data size therefore gets spurious warnings or a refusal ('Incomplete chunk ID' before data).
evidence: scipy/io/wavfile.py:515-516 and :541 (_handle_pad_byte on the declared size); corner case data-odd-size

what: wavio.read_wav refuses a WAV whose RIFF size field is 0 or too small, which is what a streaming recorder leaves before patching the header. It raises UnboundLocalError about 'fs', so a crashed recorder's capture cannot be received by either implementation (the C++ refuses identically). Patching the header size first would rescue it.
evidence: scipy/io/wavfile.py:729 'while fid.tell() < file_size' and :786; corner cases riff-size-0 and riff-size-fmt-only

what: qrss_receive.py tests 'if args.slot' and 'if args.start', so --slot '' counts as absent (a WAV then says '--slot is required for a WAV input') and --start '' is silently ignored (the default t0-12 s applies). The C++ mirrors this.
evidence: qrss_receive.py main(): q = parse_slot(args.slot) if args.slot else None; test_refusals case wav-empty-slot

what: qrss_receive.py checked --image only after the whole receive. A missing directory, or a name Pillow cannot map, raised after up to about 35 s of FULL receive, and the result was lost. Wave 7 item 7 checks it up front. The wave 7 review also refuses read-only Pillow formats (.psd, .xpm, .gbr).
evidence: First C++ FULL run printed 'FileNotFoundError: ... out/ce-full-nat.png' as Python does (render_pass saves last). Wave 7: test_cli_checks_the_image_before_receiving.

what: A slot before 1970 (q < 0) made qrss_receive.py acquire and track normally, then die with an uncaught ValueError from sequences.scrambler at the first demodulation. The C++ was worse: its demodulators cast q to uint64, descrambled with 2^64 + q and printed a pass. Fixed at three layers: the CLI guard (6b review), receive_pass's q < 0 throw (2671a6b), and parse_slot's refusal in both implementations (wave 7 item 6).
evidence: sequences.py:137 'q must fit in uint64, not {q}'; receiver.cpp:317-320 static_cast<std::uint64_t>(q). Probe: --slot 1969-12-31T23:45Z gives Python exit 1, while the C++ printed a pass before the fix. Wave 7 message: "slot 1969-12-31T23:45Z is before 1970-01-01T00:00Z".

what: load_npz trusted the archive. fs == 0 reached a ZeroDivisionError, a 2-D fe failed inside sliding_window_view with an error naming neither the file nor the member, and t0_index NaN printed a RuntimeWarning and found nothing. what: TBD_GUMBEL_MU[0] = 9.845 does not round the reference's own measurement (9.8443 rounds to 9.844). Harmless at 0.0007. The other three constants round correctly.

what: A3's Gumbel-by-moments fit is strongly conservative in the far tail. A3's real false-alarm rate at TBD_PFA is perhaps 3-10x below nominal, which costs sensitivity, not safety.

what: A1's frozen threshold is mildly anti-conservative (1.44x nominal at 1e-4, 1.20x at 1e-3), within the reference test's factor of 2. A2 is conservative. Both implementations agree.

what: PassbandStore.pack_hour's path.stat() sat outside its try. A raw hour that vanished between listing and packing raised FileNotFoundError out of the packer thread, killing that packer pass and every later hour in its list.
